assembly_notes: Full-height security turnstile. The grounded `guard_frame` part carries a floor bearing race and an overhead bearing race on one vertical spindle line, and the `rotor` part turns REVOLUTE about +Z between them through one wing sector (2*pi/wing_count either way). The rotor reach is the guard radius minus a 30 mm running clearance, so the swept envelope stays inside the guard at every angle for every guard candidate. guard_frame varies the fixed structure: an open four-post portal, the same portal infilled with horizontal side bars, a curved arc-rail cage on uprights, that cage closed into a cylinder by intermediate bars, or twin curved panels on a floor rail. header_form puts either a flat slab housing or a double-rib circular arch on posts over the upper bearing, and every bearing height, rotor span and rung pitch is re-derived from that header depth. rotor_form varies the wing: a horizontal arm ladder, that ladder braced with an outer post and diagonals, a stile-and-rung welded ladder, a dense curved-bar ladder with diagonals, or a vertical-bar palisade between two wing rails. access_control puts the reader hardware on the entry post, on a stand-off bracket with a keypad, on a free-standing outboard post with conduit and gussets, or up in the header as an indicator panel. second_mechanism adds one more real articulation: a framed service guard leaf hinged to the frame, a breakaway wing hinged to the rotor, a ratchet ring with a frame-mounted release pawl, or an overhead eccentric cam mimic-driven by the rotor with its own roller-arm follower. guard_radius_m, overall_height_m and spindle_radius_m are the honest continuous parameters; wing_count, tier_count and guard_member_count are the multiplicities; palette and decorative counts are neither. Host adaptation: when second_mechanism is emergency_breakaway_wing the rotor grows a 100 mm hub drum and every wing on that rotor starts from the drum instead of the spindle, so the breakaway wing can hinge on its own vertical stile 11 mm off the drum and still fold clear of its neighbour. Both bearing races are tied back to the guard by a floor ring and a head ring plus radial braces and one tie per repeated guard member, so the fixed body stays welded together for every guard candidate.

multiplicities.host_capacity_expression: 3 <= wing_count <= 4; the guard arc and the rotor motion limits are both 2*pi/wing_count so every sector keeps a full passage opening
multiplicities.name: wing_count
multiplicities.spacing_expression: wing i is placed at i * 2*pi/wing_count around the spindle

multiplicities.host_capacity_expression: 6 <= tier_count <= 11; adjacent members keep at least 90 mm of clear pitch at the shortest rotor span
multiplicities.name: tier_count
multiplicities.spacing_expression: ladder rotors put rung j at wing_z0_m + j * tier_pitch_m up the wing; the palisade rotor spreads the same count of vertical bars radially between the two wing rails

multiplicities.host_capacity_expression: 5 <= guard_member_count <= 12; the member half-width is min(0.030, 0.45 * guard_radius_m * guard_member_pitch_rad), so adjacent members always keep at least half the member pitch as clear arc
multiplicities.name: guard_member_count
multiplicities.spacing_expression: member k sits at -guard_arc_rad/2 + k * guard_member_pitch_rad on the guard radius, or at the matching station of the portal perimeter

candidates.notes: Portal guards use a flat full-width leaf. Arc and cylindrical guards derive a complementary front-arc leaf from the guard opening. The hinge may occupy either outlet edge; its axis sign mirrors with hinge_side so positive travel always opens outward.

parameters.name: service_leaf_hinge_side
parameters.rationale: Either outlet jamb can carry the service leaf; the hinge axis sign and leaf extent mirror together so the positive revolute direction always opens away from the guarded passage.
